games.title: Why This Material?
games.skillName: Giving reasons for the uses of everyday materials
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials, including metals, wood and plastic
games.instruction: Think about the material's properties, then tap the best reason.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the object has to do, then try again.

questions.ask: Why are saucepans made of metal?
Why are saucepan handles often made of plastic or wood?
Why are the wires inside a cable made of copper?
Why is a plastic coating put around electrical wires?
Why are windows made of glass?
Why is wood a good material for a garden bench?
Why are raincoats made of plastic-coated fabric?
In a fair test, a plastic spoon stayed coolest in hot water. What does that show?
A fair test showed kitchen roll soaked up the most water. What is it best used for?
Why does a fridge magnet stick to a steel door but not a wooden one?
